newsitem.title: GERMANY: Viag jumps on BT, MCI merger news.
newsitem.headline: Viag jumps on BT, MCI merger news.

text.p: Shares in German mixed utility Viag AG, British Telecommunications Plc's partner in Germany, rose on Monday, following confirmation of a merger between BT and U.S. firm MCI Communications.
Viag was up 6.50 marks, or over one percent, at 572 marks, while the DAX index of 30 leading shares slipped 0.64 percent to 2,666.04 points.
But on Sunday, Viag said the merger would have very little effect on the current partnership with BT.
Dealers said Viag had a lot of catching up to do with German utility competitors, Veba and RWE, who are in alliance with the Britain's Cable and Wireless.
In October, Viag shares dropped after the sudden departure of RWE from its telecoms alliance with BT.
Both RWE and Veba were slightly weaker on Monday, but firmer than the market trend. RWE was down 10 pfennigs at 62.90 marks, while Veba was down 55 pfennigs at 81.05 marks.
